sections.h2: Fuel VAT and liquor excise supply 34% of state own-tax revenue, outside GST

chart.title: Fuel VAT is the second-largest state tax after SGST, ahead of liquor excise
chart.sub: Share of national own-tax revenue, 2025-26 budget estimates, %.
chart.source: PRS Legislative Research, State of State Finances 2025, Figure 20.

sections.means: Fuel VAT and liquor excise together make up a third of what states raise themselves, from two commodities outside GST.
sections.todo: Treat petrol and diesel as roughly a fifth of state own-tax revenue in any GST Council decision about them.

sections.h2: Telangana, Meghalaya and Andhra Pradesh each draw about 44% from fuel and liquor

chart.title: Arunachal Pradesh's fuel and liquor share is over half its own-tax revenue
chart.sub: Fuel VAT plus liquor excise as a share of each state's own-tax revenue, %.
chart.source: PRS Legislative Research, State of State Finances 2025, Figure 20.

sections.means: Kerala's 40.6% runs mostly through fuel VAT at 2.4% of GSDP, while its liquor excise is only 0.2%.
sections.todo: Compare states on their fuel and liquor shares together with each state's own-tax total, not on either line alone.

sections.h2: Bihar, Mizoram and Nagaland collect no liquor excise under prohibition

chart.title: Under prohibition the liquor excise line falls to zero
chart.sub: State excise on liquor, % of GSDP, 2025-26 budget estimates.
chart.source: PRS Legislative Research, State of State Finances 2025, Figure 20.

sections.means: Bihar's fuel-plus-liquor share is just 18.2%, with fuel VAT at 1.0% of GSDP and no excise.
sections.todo: Model a prohibition state's revenue on fuel VAT alone, not on a combined fuel-and-liquor base.
